# Session Summary

Condensed arc of the work in this repo. Source of truth is `session_status.md`
(append-only log, ~1200 lines). This file is a high-level export covering
2026-02-24 through 2026-03-05.

The project began as an LLM-driven HTML5 game generator (Asteroids), then
pivoted on 2026-02-26 into a literate C++ emulator for the Stern Berzerk
arcade machine (1980), with MAME as the authoritative blueprint.

---

## Part 1 -- LLM Game Generator (2026-02-24, archived)

Single-day workstream that produced a working CLI generator and was then
mothballed when the project pivoted.

- Phase 1-5 in one day: config/LLM client, Docker sandbox, orchestrator
  pipeline, web UI (later removed), build scripts, 15 passing tests
- Iterated through three LLM API shapes: OpenAI chat completions ->
  ScalarLM `/v1/generate` -> back to chat completions -> finally the
  `scalarlm` Python package with Qwen chat-template prompts
- Stub mode (`--stub`) added to serve a bundled jsocol/asteroids without
  any LLM call
- Fixed a Docker port-mapping race in `sandbox/manager.py` (retry loop
  around `container.reload()`)
- Hygiene: `.gitignore`, `black` pre-commit, README, docstrings

Surviving artifacts: `llm/`, `orchestrator/`, `sandbox/` directories.

---

## Part 2 -- Berzerk Emulator (2026-02-26 onward)

Literate C++ (noweb) emulator. 8 phases planned; phases 0-7 complete,
phase 8 in progress.

### Phase 0+1 -- Infrastructure and MAME Analysis (2026-02-26)
- Studied MAME `berzerk.cpp` driver and Z80 CPU core
- Wrote `cdoc/architecture.md` -- comprehensive hardware reference
- Created `Dockerfile` (Ubuntu 24.04, g++, noweb, texlive, SDL2, gdb)
- Created `Makefile` (tangle/weave/build/clean/docker-* targets)
- Validated tangle -> compile -> run and weave -> PDF pipelines

### Phase 2 -- Memory Subsystem
- `noweb/memory.nw` -- AddressSpace with read/write callbacks
- Berzerk memory map: ROM/CMOS RAM/scratch RAM/VRAM/Magic RAM/Color RAM
- ROM loader for 8 RC31A revision files (CRC verified)

### Phase 3 -- Z80 CPU (2026-02-26)
- `noweb/z80.nw` -- ~2700 lines, all 256 unprefixed + CB/ED/DD/FD/DDCB/FDCB
- PAIR16 register unions (MAME pattern), composed flag byte with lookup tables
- Full interrupt handling (NMI + IM 0/1/2), HALT, EI delay, WZ/MEMPTR
- Integrated `SingleStepTests/z80` JSON suite (1604 files, ~1.6M tests)
- After Q-register tracking + several rounds of fixes:
  **1,604,000 / 1,604,000 tests passing (100%)**

### Phase 4 -- Video, Magic RAM, Sound, Interrupts (2026-02-27)
- `video.nw`: VideoState (8KB VRAM + 2KB color RAM + framebuffer),
  `render_frame()` matching MAME's `screen_update`, full 74181 ALU
  pipeline, collision detection (intercept flip-flop), `bitswap8`
- `sound.nw`: S14001A speech and Exidy 6840 timer stubs (correct
  register behavior so polling loops don't hang)
- `interrupts.nw`: 2 IRQs + 8 NMIs per frame at scanline-accurate cycle
  offsets, `run_frame()` chunked execution between events

### Phase 5 -- SDL Platform + noVNC Browser (2026-02-27)
- `platform.nw`: SDL2 window/renderer/texture, input mapping
  (arrows/ctrl/space/1/2/5/esc -> port 0x48/0x49/0x4A bits)
- `Dockerfile.novnc` + `scripts/start-novnc.sh`: Xvfb -> x11vnc ->
  noVNC at `localhost:6080/vnc.html`
- `make docker-play` end-to-end target

#### 74181 ALU bug (memorable fix)
Game stuck at PC=0x0458 in Magic RAM self-test. The per-bit output was
`(!p) & g`; correct equation is `1 ^ ((!p) & g)`. Without the XOR,
S=0000 produced F=A (identity) instead of F=~A (complement), so every
ALU configuration produced wrong VRAM. After fix: game boots, passes
self-tests, reaches attract mode, user-confirmed in browser.

### Phase 6 -- Disassembly Documentation + Static Analysis (2026-03-05)
Two-track effort: machine-verified disassembly + opcode-level deep
traces of every major subsystem.

- `scripts/z80_disasm.py` -- independent Z80 disassembler/verifier
  - Byte verification: 5432/5432 (100%)
  - Instruction decode: 5286/5293 (99.87%, remainder are formatting
    differences vs Tunstall's negative-decimal notation)
  - Static analysis: 119 verified subroutine entry points, 877 branch
    targets, 139 data regions
- `cdoc/disassembly.md` -- master reference (opcode-verified)
- `cdoc/disassembly_analysis.md` -- 47 RAM variables, struct layouts,
  60+ subroutines, 10 algorithms with pseudocode, complete I/O port map
- `cdoc/phase6_structs_rendering.md` -- VECTOR (14 bytes), BOLT
  (8 bytes), LINKED_LIST_ITEM (6 bytes incl. negative-offset next-ptrs),
  sprite/pattern double-indirection format, 11-step bottom-of-screen
  rendering pipeline
- `cdoc/phase6_maze_robots_difficulty.md` -- maze gen ($2540), robot
  spawning ($2117, 11-slot 4-3-4 grid), difficulty tables ($3794),
  74181 ALU truth table
- `cdoc/phase6_jobs_otto_rooms.md` -- cooperative job scheduler
  (stack-based coroutines), Evil Otto AI, room transitions, demo mode
- `noweb/disassembly.nw` (9797 lines) -- literate version of Tunstall's
  disassembly, 36 functional sections, tangles bit-identical to original
- RNG correction: traced opcodes at $267E-$2681 and confirmed
  `seed * 7 + $3153` (prior memory said *5*)

### Phase 7 -- Cosimulation Infrastructure (2026-03-05)
Verifies a second implementation by running it side-by-side with the
emulator and comparing per-frame logs.

- `noweb/cosim.nw` -- `BerzerkMachine` abstract interface
  (init/reset/step_frame/snapshot/restore/set_input/take_frame_log),
  `MachineSnapshot` (full Z80 + RAM + VRAM + color RAM + magic state),
  `EventRecord` (memory/io/collision events tagged by region)
- `noweb/emulator.nw` -- `BerzerkEmulator : BerzerkMachine` wrapping
  the existing engine. `EventLogger` is flag-gated (zero overhead when
  disabled), tags ISR-entered routines as INTERRUPT vs CONVENTIONAL
- `noweb/cosim_harness.nw` -- `CosimRunner`, set-based event comparison
  (intra-frame ordering may differ between implementations), ordered
  invocation-sequence comparison, binary input-recording format
- Correctness model: comparison at subroutine boundaries, not cycle
  boundaries. Frame-level pixel/sound equality, but intra-frame side
  effects compared as sets unless writes target the same address
- Cross-platform Makefile fix: replaced Linux-only `grep -oP` with
  `grep -oE` + `sed`

### Phase 8 -- Native C++ Reimplementation (in progress)
Second `BerzerkMachine` implementation written from Phase 6 docs, not
disassembly tangle. Verified bit-accurate against the emulator via
Phase 7 cosim harness.

#### Implemented and cosim-verified
- RNG, maze generation (border + interior walls, doorway gaps)
- `CALCULATE_MAGIC_IMAGE_RAM_ADDRESS` ($29A3) -- with corrected
  $6400 base address (32-line vblank offset)
- `PRINT_CHAR` / `PRINT_DIGITS` / `SHOW_SCORE` / draw_lives /
  `colour_fill` / post-maze rendering ($2597-$25C9)
- Sprite pipeline: `draw_sprite` (1- and 2-byte modes),
  `erase_pattern`, `write_pattern` (XOR mode + collision via port $4E),
  `move_animate_vector` (TIME/TPRIME, velocity, frame cycling)
- Cosim test (`noweb/cosim_test.nw`): RNG determinism, maze determinism,
  full $2540 maze+colour+lives+score against Z80 emulator -- **0 VRAM
  mismatches, 843 non-zero bytes match exactly, no ROM patches needed**

#### Bugs found and fixed during cosim
1. Coordinate base address $6000 vs $6400 (vblank offset)
2. VRAM/coord write ordering (clear VRAM before writing coords)
3. Visible-region comparison ($0400-$1FFF only -- the vblank scanlines
   $0000-$03FF are scratch RAM for game variables: ROOM_X, RNG_SEED,
   maze config)
4. ROM function scope ($2540 continues into colour setup, lives, score)
5. Memory-map discovery: VRAM is $4000-$5FFF (not $6000), Magic RAM at
   $6000-$7FFF mirrors VRAM through 74181 ALU

#### Still TODO
Robot AI (SEEK / SETPAT / SET_VELOCITY), robot explosion (BLAM), robot
shooting, player bolts (FIRE / MOVE_AND_DRAW_BOLT), collision detection
hookup, Evil Otto, BCD scoring, colour attributes (COLOUR_MAN /
UNCOLOUR_MAN, wall colours), full game-loop scheduler, multi-frame
cosim with moving sprites.

---

## Verification at end of session window

- Z80 instruction tests: 1,604,000 / 1,604,000 passing
- Memory self-test: passing
- Native build: clean (g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra, zero warnings)
- `make docker-play`: game boots, attract mode visible in browser,
  user-confirmed playable
- Maze generation cosim: 0 VRAM mismatches against emulator

## Project layout

```
noweb/          literate sources (.nw)
src/, include/  tangled C++ (gitignored)
doc/            woven PDFs (gitignored)
cdoc/           hand-written design docs and disassembly analysis
scripts/        z80_disasm.py, gen_disasm_nw.py, start-novnc.sh
rom/berzerk/    8 ROM files (RC31A + voice ROMs)
third_party/    nlohmann/json.hpp, SingleStepTests/z80
```

## Key build commands

- `make build` -- tangle + compile inside Docker
- `make docker-play` -- noVNC browser session at localhost:6080/vnc.html
- `make docker-test-z80` -- run the 1.6M-test Z80 suite
- `make docker-cosim-test` -- run native vs emulator cosim
- `make weave` -- generate PDF documentation

499	### What the loop at 0x0456-0x0459 is doing
500	
501	This is a Magic RAM verification/polling loop. The sequence that precedes it:
502	- OUT (0x4B),A   sets the Magic RAM control register (ALU configuration)
503	- LD (HL),0xFF   writes 0xFF through the Magic RAM ALU -> result lands in VRAM[HL-0x2000]
504	- LD (HL),D      writes D through ALU (second pass, shifts the 74181 pipeline)
505	- LD (HL),0x00   writes 0x00 through ALU
506	
507	Then the loop:
508	```
509	.poll: LD A,(HL)   ; read back VRAM to check what the ALU wrote
510	       CP E        ; compare against expected result in E
511	       JR NZ,.poll ; spin until VRAM matches expectation
512	```
513	
514	This is a read-back completion poll, verifying that the Magic RAM ALU pipeline
515	has fully committed its result to underlying VRAM before the CPU proceeds.
516	The 74181 ALU pipeline could have timing slack vs CPU; the loop ensures
517	the result is stable. This is the hardware self-test / initialization
518	of the Magic RAM unit, not a data-driven game loop.

521	through the carry each pass, testing each of the 16 possible ALU configurations
522	(or 16 pixel patterns). When all 16 passes complete (carry falls out of D),
523	it jumps away to further boot initialization.

531	## 2026-02-27: MAME magicram_w XOR 0xFF Research
532	
533	### Question
534	Does MAME's magicram_w invert the 74181 ALU output before storing to VRAM?
535	Does MAME's 74181 device have active-low F outputs?
536	
537	### Findings -- magicram_w (src/mame/stern/berzerk.cpp)
538	
539	Exact code fetched from MAME master:
540	
541	```cpp
542	void berzerk_state::magicram_w(offs_t offset, uint8_t data)
543	{
544	    uint8_t alu_output;
545	    uint8_t current_video_data = m_videoram[offset];
546	
547	    uint8_t shift_flop_output = (((uint16_t)m_last_shift_data << 8) | data) >> (m_magicram_control & 0x07);
548	
549	    if (m_magicram_control & 0x08)
550	        shift_flop_output = bitswap<8>(shift_flop_output, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7);
551	
552	    if (shift_flop_output & current_video_data)
553	        m_intercept = 0;
554	
555	    m_ls181_12c->input_a_w(shift_flop_output >> 0);
556	    m_ls181_10c->input_a_w(shift_flop_output >> 4);
557	    m_ls181_12c->input_b_w(current_video_data >> 0);
558	    m_ls181_10c->input_b_w(current_video_data >> 4);
559	    m_ls181_12c->select_w(m_magicram_control >> 4);
560	    m_ls181_10c->select_w(m_magicram_control >> 4);
561	
562	    alu_output = m_ls181_10c->function_r() << 4 | m_ls181_12c->function_r();
563	
564	    m_videoram[offset] = alu_output ^ 0xff;   // <-- XOR 0xFF inversion IS present
565	
566	    m_last_shift_data = data & 0x7f;
567	}
568	```
569	
570	### Findings -- 74181 device (src/devices/machine/74181.cpp)
571	
572	The `function_r()` method returns `m_f` directly.
573	`m_f` is assigned as: `m_f = fp0 | fp1 << 1 | fp2 << 2 | fp3 << 3`
574	There is NO inversion inside the 74181 device itself.
575	There is NO active-low mode, no separate Y output, no XOR inside function_r().
576	
577	### Answer
578	
579	YES -- the XOR 0xFF is in magicram_w, applied AFTER reading the (active-high) F output
580	from MAME's 74181 emulation device. The 74181 device returns an active-high result;
581	the inversion lives in the Berzerk driver, not in the chip model. This matches the
582	real hardware: the 74181's F outputs are open-collector active-low on the Berzerk PCB,
583	so MAME models the chip with active-high outputs and the driver inverts the result
584	to reproduce the correct VRAM value.
585	
586	### Implication for our implementation
587	Our `ttl74181_logic()` in video.nw must return the active-high value (no inversion
588	inside the function), and `magic_ram_write()` must apply `^ 0xFF` after combining
589	the two nibble results -- exactly matching MAME's pattern.

591	## 2026-02-27: 74181 ALU Bug Fix -- Game Now Boots
592	
593	### Bug
594	Game stuck at PC=0x0458 in Magic RAM self-test loop. The boot code writes
595	three values through Magic RAM, reads back VRAM, and compares against an
596	expected result. VRAM[0x0000] was 0xFF but game expected 0x00.
597	
598	### Root Cause
599	In `ttl74181_logic()` (video.nw), the per-bit output equation was:
600	```
601	fi = (!p) & g
602	```
603	This computes the P/G intermediate terms correctly but is MISSING the
604	XOR with the carry input term. MAME's equation is:
605	```
606	fp = !(Cn & mp) XOR ((!ap) & bp)
607	```
608	In logic mode (M=1), mp=0, so the carry term simplifies to 1. The correct
609	equation is:
610	```
611	fi = 1 XOR ((!p) & g)
612	```
613	Without the `1 XOR`, select S=0000 produced F=A (identity) instead of
614	F=~A (complement). This caused every ALU configuration to produce wrong
615	results.
616	
617	### Fix
618	Changed line in video.nw ttl74181_logic:
619	```
620	- int fi = (!p) & g;
621	+ int fi = 1 ^ ((!p) & g);
622	```

499	### What the loop at 0x0456-0x0459 is doing
500	
501	This is a Magic RAM verification/polling loop. The sequence that precedes it:
502	- OUT (0x4B),A   sets the Magic RAM control register (ALU configuration)
503	- LD (HL),0xFF   writes 0xFF through the Magic RAM ALU -> result lands in VRAM[HL-0x2000]
504	- LD (HL),D      writes D through ALU (second pass, shifts the 74181 pipeline)
505	- LD (HL),0x00   writes 0x00 through ALU
506	
507	Then the loop:
508	```
509	.poll: LD A,(HL)   ; read back VRAM to check what the ALU wrote
510	       CP E        ; compare against expected result in E
511	       JR NZ,.poll ; spin until VRAM matches expectation
512	```
513	
514	This is a read-back completion poll, verifying that the Magic RAM ALU pipeline
515	has fully committed its result to underlying VRAM before the CPU proceeds.
516	The 74181 ALU pipeline could have timing slack vs CPU; the loop ensures
517	the result is stable. This is the hardware self-test / initialization
518	of the Magic RAM unit, not a data-driven game loop.

520	The outer structure (0x045C-0x0465) iterates 0x10 (16) times, rotating D

531	## 2026-02-27: MAME magicram_w XOR 0xFF Research
532	
533	### Question
534	Does MAME's magicram_w invert the 74181 ALU output before storing to VRAM?
535	Does MAME's 74181 device have active-low F outputs?
536	
537	### Findings -- magicram_w (src/mame/stern/berzerk.cpp)
538	
539	Exact code fetched from MAME master:
540	
541	```cpp
542	void berzerk_state::magicram_w(offs_t offset, uint8_t data)
543	{
544	    uint8_t alu_output;
545	    uint8_t current_video_data = m_videoram[offset];
546	
547	    uint8_t shift_flop_output = (((uint16_t)m_last_shift_data << 8) | data) >> (m_magicram_control & 0x07);
548	
549	    if (m_magicram_control & 0x08)
550	        shift_flop_output = bitswap<8>(shift_flop_output, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7);
551	
552	    if (shift_flop_output & current_video_data)
553	        m_intercept = 0;
554	
555	    m_ls181_12c->input_a_w(shift_flop_output >> 0);
556	    m_ls181_10c->input_a_w(shift_flop_output >> 4);
557	    m_ls181_12c->input_b_w(current_video_data >> 0);
558	    m_ls181_10c->input_b_w(current_video_data >> 4);
559	    m_ls181_12c->select_w(m_magicram_control >> 4);
560	    m_ls181_10c->select_w(m_magicram_control >> 4);
561	
562	    alu_output = m_ls181_10c->function_r() << 4 | m_ls181_12c->function_r();
563	
564	    m_videoram[offset] = alu_output ^ 0xff;   // <-- XOR 0xFF inversion IS present
565	
566	    m_last_shift_data = data & 0x7f;
567	}
568	```
569	
570	### Findings -- 74181 device (src/devices/machine/74181.cpp)
571	
572	The `function_r()` method returns `m_f` directly.
573	`m_f` is assigned as: `m_f = fp0 | fp1 << 1 | fp2 << 2 | fp3 << 3`
574	There is NO inversion inside the 74181 device itself.
575	There is NO active-low mode, no separate Y output, no XOR inside function_r().
576	
577	### Answer
578	
579	YES -- the XOR 0xFF is in magicram_w, applied AFTER reading the (active-high) F output
580	from MAME's 74181 emulation device. The 74181 device returns an active-high result;
581	the inversion lives in the Berzerk driver, not in the chip model. This matches the
582	real hardware: the 74181's F outputs are open-collector active-low on the Berzerk PCB,
583	so MAME models the chip with active-high outputs and the driver inverts the result
584	to reproduce the correct VRAM value.
585	
586	### Implication for our implementation
587	Our `ttl74181_logic()` in video.nw must return the active-high value (no inversion
588	inside the function), and `magic_ram_write()` must apply `^ 0xFF` after combining
589	the two nibble results -- exactly matching MAME's pattern.

591	## 2026-02-27: 74181 ALU Bug Fix -- Game Now Boots
592	
593	### Bug
594	Game stuck at PC=0x0458 in Magic RAM self-test loop. The boot code writes
595	three values through Magic RAM, reads back VRAM, and compares against an
596	expected result. VRAM[0x0000] was 0xFF but game expected 0x00.
597	
598	### Root Cause
599	In `ttl74181_logic()` (video.nw), the per-bit output equation was:
600	```
601	fi = (!p) & g
602	```
603	This computes the P/G intermediate terms correctly but is MISSING the
604	XOR with the carry input term. MAME's equation is:
605	```
606	fp = !(Cn & mp) XOR ((!ap) & bp)
607	```
608	In logic mode (M=1), mp=0, so the carry term simplifies to 1. The correct
609	equation is:
610	```
611	fi = 1 XOR ((!p) & g)
612	```
613	Without the `1 XOR`, select S=0000 produced F=A (identity) instead of
614	F=~A (complement). This caused every ALU configuration to produce wrong
615	results.
616	
617	### Fix
618	Changed line in video.nw ttl74181_logic:
619	```
620	- int fi = (!p) & g;
621	+ int fi = 1 ^ ((!p) & g);
622	```

input.content:
# Session Summary

Condensed arc of the work in this repo. Source of truth is `session_status.md`
(append-only log, ~1200 lines). This file is a high-level export covering
2026-02-24 through 2026-03-05.

The project began as an LLM-driven HTML5 game generator (Asteroids), then
pivoted on 2026-02-26 into a literate C++ emulator for the Stern Berzerk
arcade machine (1980), with MAME as the authoritative blueprint.

---

## Part 1 -- LLM Game Generator (2026-02-24, archived)

Single-day workstream that produced a working CLI generator and was then
mothballed when the project pivoted.

- Phase 1-5 in one day: config/LLM client, Docker sandbox, orchestrator
  pipeline, web UI (later removed), build scripts, 15 passing tests
- Iterated through three LLM API shapes: OpenAI chat completions ->
  ScalarLM `/v1/generate` -> back to chat completions -> finally the
  `scalarlm` Python package with Qwen chat-template prompts
- Stub mode (`--stub`) added to serve a bundled jsocol/asteroids without
  any LLM call
- Fixed a Docker port-mapping race in `sandbox/manager.py` (retry loop
  around `container.reload()`)
- Hygiene: `.gitignore`, `black` pre-commit, README, docstrings

Surviving artifacts: `llm/`, `orchestrator/`, `sandbox/` directories.

---

## Part 2 -- Berzerk Emulator (2026-02-26 onward)

Literate C++ (noweb) emulator. 8 phases planned; phases 0-7 complete,
phase 8 in progress.

### Phase 0+1 -- Infrastructure and MAME Analysis (2026-02-26)
- Studied MAME `berzerk.cpp` driver and Z80 CPU core
- Wrote `cdoc/architecture.md` -- comprehensive hardware reference
- Created `Dockerfile` (Ubuntu 24.04, g++, noweb, texlive, SDL2, gdb)
- Created `Makefile` (tangle/weave/build/clean/docker-* targets)
- Validated tangle -> compile -> run and weave -> PDF pipelines

### Phase 2 -- Memory Subsystem
- `noweb/memory.nw` -- AddressSpace with read/write callbacks
- Berzerk memory map: ROM/CMOS RAM/scratch RAM/VRAM/Magic RAM/Color RAM
- ROM loader for 8 RC31A revision files (CRC verified)

### Phase 3 -- Z80 CPU (2026-02-26)
- `noweb/z80.nw` -- ~2700 lines, all 256 unprefixed + CB/ED/DD/FD/DDCB/FDCB
- PAIR16 register unions (MAME pattern), composed flag byte with lookup tables
- Full interrupt handling (NMI + IM 0/1/2), HALT, EI delay, WZ/MEMPTR
- Integrated `SingleStepTests/z80` JSON suite (1604 files, ~1.6M tests)
- After Q-register tracking + several rounds of fixes:
  **1,604,000 / 1,604,000 tests passing (100%)**

### Phase 4 -- Video, Magic RAM, Sound, Interrupts (2026-02-27)
- `video.nw`: VideoState (8KB VRAM + 2KB color RAM + framebuffer),
  `render_frame()` matching MAME's `screen_update`, full 74181 ALU
  pipeline, collision detection (intercept flip-flop), `bitswap8`
- `sound.nw`: S14001A speech and Exidy 6840 timer stubs (correct
  register behavior so polling loops don't hang)
- `interrupts.nw`: 2 IRQs + 8 NMIs per frame at scanline-accurate cycle
  offsets, `run_frame()` chunked execution between events

### Phase 5 -- SDL Platform + noVNC Browser (2026-02-27)
- `platform.nw`: SDL2 window/renderer/texture, input mapping
  (arrows/ctrl/space/1/2/5/esc -> port 0x48/0x49/0x4A bits)
- `Dockerfile.novnc` + `scripts/start-novnc.sh`: Xvfb -> x11vnc ->
  noVNC at `localhost:6080/vnc.html`
- `make docker-play` end-to-end target

#### 74181 ALU bug (memorable fix)
Game stuck at PC=0x0458 in Magic RAM self-test. The per-bit output was
`(!p) & g`; correct equation is `1 ^ ((!p) & g)`. Without the XOR,
S=0000 produced F=A (identity) instead of F=~A (complement), so every
ALU configuration produced wrong VRAM. After fix: game boots, passes
self-tests, reaches attract mode, user-confirmed in browser.

### Phase 6 -- Disassembly Documentation + Static Analysis (2026-03-05)
Two-track effort: machine-verified disassembly + opcode-level deep
traces of every major subsystem.

- `scripts/z80_disasm.py` -- independent Z80 disassembler/verifier
  - Byte verification: 5432/5432 (100%)
  - Instruction decode: 5286/5293 (99.87%, remainder are formatting
    differences vs Tunstall's negative-decimal notation)
  - Static analysis: 119 verified subroutine entry points, 877 branch
    targets, 139 data regions
- `cdoc/disassembly.md` -- master reference (opcode-verified)
- `cdoc/disassembly_analysis.md` -- 47 RAM variables, struct layouts,
  60+ subroutines, 10 algorithms with pseudocode, complete I/O port map
- `cdoc/phase6_structs_rendering.md` -- VECTOR (14 bytes), BOLT
  (8 bytes), LINKED_LIST_ITEM (6 bytes incl. negative-offset next-ptrs),
  sprite/pattern double-indirection format, 11-step bottom-of-screen
  rendering pipeline
- `cdoc/phase6_maze_robots_difficulty.md` -- maze gen ($2540), robot
  spawning ($2117, 11-slot 4-3-4 grid), difficulty tables ($3794),
  74181 ALU truth table
- `cdoc/phase6_jobs_otto_rooms.md` -- cooperative job scheduler
  (stack-based coroutines), Evil Otto AI, room transitions, demo mode
- `noweb/disassembly.nw` (9797 lines) -- literate version of Tunstall's
  disassembly, 36 functional sections, tangles bit-identical to original
- RNG correction: traced opcodes at $267E-$2681 and confirmed
  `seed * 7 + $3153` (prior memory said *5*)

### Phase 7 -- Cosimulation Infrastructure (2026-03-05)
Verifies a second implementation by running it side-by-side with the
emulator and comparing per-frame logs.

- `noweb/cosim.nw` -- `BerzerkMachine` abstract interface
  (init/reset/step_frame/snapshot/restore/set_input/take_frame_log),
  `MachineSnapshot` (full Z80 + RAM + VRAM + color RAM + magic state),
  `EventRecord` (memory/io/collision events tagged by region)
- `noweb/emulator.nw` -- `BerzerkEmulator : BerzerkMachine` wrapping
  the existing engine. `EventLogger` is flag-gated (zero overhead when
  disabled), tags ISR-entered routines as INTERRUPT vs CONVENTIONAL
- `noweb/cosim_harness.nw` -- `CosimRunner`, set-based event comparison
  (intra-frame ordering may differ between implementations), ordered
  invocation-sequence comparison, binary input-recording format
- Correctness model: comparison at subroutine boundaries, not cycle
  boundaries. Frame-level pixel/sound equality, but intra-frame side
  effects compared as sets unless writes target the same address
- Cross-platform Makefile fix: replaced Linux-only `grep -oP` with
  `grep -oE` + `sed`

### Phase 8 -- Native C++ Reimplementation (in progress)
Second `BerzerkMachine` implementation written from Phase 6 docs, not
disassembly tangle. Verified bit-accurate against the emulator via
Phase 7 cosim harness.

#### Implemented and cosim-verified
- RNG, maze generation (border + interior walls, doorway gaps)
- `CALCULATE_MAGIC_IMAGE_RAM_ADDRESS` ($29A3) -- with corrected
  $6400 base address (32-line vblank offset)
- `PRINT_CHAR` / `PRINT_DIGITS` / `SHOW_SCORE` / draw_lives /
  `colour_fill` / post-maze rendering ($2597-$25C9)
- Sprite pipeline: `draw_sprite` (1- and 2-byte modes),
  `erase_pattern`, `write_pattern` (XOR mode + collision via port $4E),
  `move_animate_vector` (TIME/TPRIME, velocity, frame cycling)
- Cosim test (`noweb/cosim_test.nw`): RNG determinism, maze determinism,
  full $2540 maze+colour+lives+score against Z80 emulator -- **0 VRAM
  mismatches, 843 non-zero bytes match exactly, no ROM patches needed**

#### Bugs found and fixed during cosim
1. Coordinate base address $6000 vs $6400 (vblank offset)
2. VRAM/coord write ordering (clear VRAM before writing coords)
3. Visible-region comparison ($0400-$1FFF only -- the vblank scanlines
   $0000-$03FF are scratch RAM for game variables: ROOM_X, RNG_SEED,
   maze config)
4. ROM function scope ($2540 continues into colour setup, lives, score)
5. Memory-map discovery: VRAM is $4000-$5FFF (not $6000), Magic RAM at
   $6000-$7FFF mirrors VRAM through 74181 ALU

#### Still TODO
Robot AI (SEEK / SETPAT / SET_VELOCITY), robot explosion (BLAM), robot
shooting, player bolts (FIRE / MOVE_AND_DRAW_BOLT), collision detection
hookup, Evil Otto, BCD scoring, colour attributes (COLOUR_MAN /
UNCOLOUR_MAN, wall colours), full game-loop scheduler, multi-frame
cosim with moving sprites.

---

## Verification at end of session window

- Z80 instruction tests: 1,604,000 / 1,604,000 passing
- Memory self-test: passing
- Native build: clean (g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra, zero warnings)
- `make docker-play`: game boots, attract mode visible in browser,
  user-confirmed playable
- Maze generation cosim: 0 VRAM mismatches against emulator

## Project layout

```
noweb/          literate sources (.nw)
src/, include/  tangled C++ (gitignored)
doc/            woven PDFs (gitignored)
cdoc/           hand-written design docs and disassembly analysis
scripts/        z80_disasm.py, gen_disasm_nw.py, start-novnc.sh
rom/berzerk/    8 ROM files (RC31A + voice ROMs)
third_party/    nlohmann/json.hpp, SingleStepTests/z80
```

## Key build commands

- `make build` -- tangle + compile inside Docker
- `make docker-play` -- noVNC browser session at localhost:6080/vnc.html
- `make docker-test-z80` -- run the 1.6M-test Z80 suite
- `make docker-cosim-test` -- run native vs emulator cosim
- `make weave` -- generate PDF documentation

python3 <<'PY'
import json, os, datetime, re
from collections import defaultdict

PROJECT_PATH = "/Users/sudnya/checkout/smi/gfx-challenge"
PROJECT_DIR = "/Users/sudnya/.claude/projects/-Users-sudnya-checkout-smi-gfx-challenge"
HISTORY = "/Users/sudnya/.claude/history.jsonl"
OUT = os.path.join(PROJECT_PATH, "session_history.md")

# 1. Load prompts from history.jsonl
prompts_by_session = defaultdict(list)
with open(HISTORY) as f:
    for line in f:
        try:
            obj = json.loads(line)
        except:
            continue
        if obj.get("project") != PROJECT_PATH:
            continue
        sid = obj.get("sessionId", "unknown")
        ts = obj.get("timestamp", 0)
        text = obj.get("display", "")
        pasted = obj.get("pastedContents", {}) or {}
        prompts_by_session[sid].append({
            "ts": ts,
            "text": text,
            "pasted": pasted,
        })

# Sort prompts by timestamp within each session
for sid in prompts_by_session:
    prompts_by_session[sid].sort(key=lambda p: p["ts"])

# 2. Load assistant responses from per-session jsonl files
# Map: sessionId -> list of (timestamp, role, content_text)
responses_by_session = defaultdict(list)
for fname in os.listdir(PROJECT_DIR):
    if not fname.endswith(".jsonl"):
        continue
    sid = fname[:-len(".jsonl")]
    fpath = os.path.join(PROJECT_DIR, fname)
    with open(fpath) as f:
        for line in f:
            try:
                obj = json.loads(line)
            except:
                continue
            mtype = obj.get("type")
            if mtype not in ("user", "assistant"):
                continue
            if obj.get("isSidechain"):
                continue
            msg = obj.get("message", {})
            role = msg.get("role")
            content = msg.get("content")
            ts = obj.get("timestamp", "")
            # Convert ts string to epoch-ish for sorting (ISO)
            text_parts = []
            if isinstance(content, str):
                text_parts.append(content)
            elif isinstance(content, list):
                for c in content:
                    ctype = c.get("type") if isinstance(c, dict) else None
                    if ctype == "text":
                        text_parts.append(c.get("text", ""))
                    elif ctype == "thinking":
                        # skip thinking
                        pass
                    elif ctype == "tool_use":
                        name = c.get("name", "")
                        inp = c.get("input", {})
                        # Compact tool call summary
                        try:
                            inp_str = json.dumps(inp, indent=2)
                        except:
                            inp_str = str(inp)
                        if len(inp_str) > 1500:
                            inp_str = inp_str[:1500] + "\n... [truncated]"
                        text_parts.append(f"[tool_use: {name}]\n```json\n{inp_str}\n```")
                    elif ctype == "tool_result":
                        # Skip - too noisy
                        pass
            text = "\n\n".join(t for t in text_parts if t)
            if not text:
                continue
            responses_by_session[sid].append({
                "ts": ts,
                "role": role,
                "text": text,
            })

# Sort
for sid in responses_by_session:
    responses_by_session[sid].sort(key=lambda r: r["ts"])

# 3. Build session metadata: earliest timestamp for ordering
session_first_ts = {}
for sid, ps in prompts_by_session.items():
    if ps:
        session_first_ts[sid] = ps[0]["ts"]
for sid, rs in responses_by_session.items():
    if rs and sid not in session_first_ts:
        # parse ISO time
        try:
            session_first_ts[sid] = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(rs[0]["ts"].replace("Z","+00:00")).timestamp() * 1000
        except:
            session_first_ts[sid] = 0

all_sids = sorted(session_first_ts.keys(), key=lambda s: session_first_ts[s])

def fmt_epoch_ms(ms):
    try:
        return datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(ms/1000.0).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    except:
        return str(ms)

def fmt_iso(s):
    try:
        return datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z","+00:00")).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC")
    except:
        return s

# 4. Compose markdown
lines = []
lines.append("# Berzerk Repository — Session History")
lines.append("")
lines.append("Compiled from Claude Code logs at `~/.claude/history.jsonl` (user prompts) and")
lines.append("`~/.claude/projects/-Users-sudnya-checkout-smi-gfx-challenge/<sessionId>.jsonl` (full")
lines.append("conversations, where available).")
lines.append("")
lines.append(f"- Project path: `{PROJECT_PATH}`")
lines.append(f"- Total sessions: {len(all_sids)}")
lines.append(f"- Total user prompts captured: {sum(len(p) for p in prompts_by_session.values())}")
lines.append(f"- Sessions with full assistant transcripts: {sum(1 for s in all_sids if responses_by_session.get(s))}")
lines.append("")
lines.append("Older sessions (pre-format change) only retain user prompts in the global history;")
lines.append("their assistant responses are not recoverable. Sub-agent traces exist for some")
lines.append("of those sessions but are not included here.")
lines.append("")
lines.append("---")
lines.append("")

for idx, sid in enumerate(all_sids, 1):
    ps = prompts_by_session.get(sid, [])
    rs = responses_by_session.get(sid, [])
    first_ts = session_first_ts[sid]
    lines.append(f"## Session {idx}: `{sid}`")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"- First activity: {fmt_epoch_ms(first_ts)}")
    lines.append(f"- User prompts: {len(ps)}")
    lines.append(f"- Assistant transcript available: {'yes' if rs else 'no (prompts only)'}")
    lines.append("")
    if rs:
        # Use full transcript order from session jsonl
        lines.append("### Full transcript")
        lines.append("")
        for entry in rs:
            role = entry["role"]
            text = entry["text"]
            ts = fmt_iso(entry["ts"])
            heading = "User" if role == "user" else "Assistant"
            lines.append(f"#### {heading} — {ts}")
            lines.append("")
            # Use blockquote for user, plain for assistant
            if role == "user":
                for ln in text.splitlines() or [""]:
                    lines.append(f"> {ln}")
                lines.append("")
            else:
                lines.append(text)
                lines.append("")
    else:
        # Prompts only
        lines.append("### User prompts (chronological)")
        lines.append("")
        for i, p in enumerate(ps, 1):
            ts = fmt_epoch_ms(p["ts"])
            lines.append(f"#### Prompt {i} — {ts}")
            lines.append("")
            for ln in (p["text"] or "").splitlines() or [""]:
                lines.append(f"> {ln}")
            lines.append("")
            if p["pasted"]:
                for pid, pdata in (p["pasted"] or {}).items():
                    if isinstance(pdata, dict):
                        ptype = pdata.get("type", "text")
                        pcontent = pdata.get("content", "")
                        lines.append(f"<details><summary>Pasted content #{pid} ({ptype})</summary>")
                        lines.append("")
                        lines.append("```")
                        lines.append(pcontent)
                        lines.append("```")
                        lines.append("")
                        lines.append("</details>")
                        lines.append("")
    lines.append("---")
    lines.append("")

out_text = "\n".join(lines)
with open(OUT, "w") as f:
    f.write(out_text)

print(f"Wrote {OUT}")
print(f"Size: {os.path.getsize(OUT)} bytes")
print(f"Lines: {len(lines)}")

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request

content.text:
I have a clear picture now. Here's the situation:
- 156 user prompts across 12 sessions are stored in `~/.claude/history.jsonl`
- Only 4 of the 12 sessions have full conversation logs (top-level `.jsonl` files) with assistant responses
- The other 8 sessions (older format) only have user prompts preserved, plus subagent traces

Let me build the markdown document.

input.command:
python3 <<'PY'
import json, os, datetime, re
from collections import defaultdict

PROJECT_PATH = "/Users/sudnya/checkout/smi/gfx-challenge"
PROJECT_DIR = "/Users/sudnya/.claude/projects/-Users-sudnya-checkout-smi-gfx-challenge"
HISTORY = "/Users/sudnya/.claude/history.jsonl"
OUT = os.path.join(PROJECT_PATH, "session_history.md")

# 1. Load prompts from history.jsonl
prompts_by_session = defaultdict(list)
with open(HISTORY) as f:
    for line in f:
        try:
            obj = json.loads(line)
        except:
            continue
        if obj.get("project") != PROJECT_PATH:
            continue
        sid = obj.get("sessionId", "unknown")
        ts = obj.get("timestamp", 0)
        text = obj.get("display", "")
        pasted = obj.get("pastedContents", {}) or {}
        prompts_by_session[sid].append({
            "ts": ts,
            "text": text,
            "pasted": pasted,
        })

# Sort prompts by timestamp within each session
for sid in prompts_by_session:
    prompts_by_session[sid].sort(key=lambda p: p["ts"])

# 2. Load assistant responses from per-session jsonl files
# Map: sessionId -> list of (timestamp, role, content_text)
responses_by_session = defaultdict(list)
for fname in os.listdir(PROJECT_DIR):
    if not fname.endswith(".jsonl"):
        continue
    sid = fname[:-len(".jsonl")]
    fpath = os.path.join(PROJECT_DIR, fname)
    with open(fpath) as f:
        for line in f:
            try:
                obj = json.loads(line)
            except:
                continue
            mtype = obj.get("type")
            if mtype not in ("user", "assistant"):
                continue
            if obj.get("isSidechain"):
                continue
            msg = obj.get("message", {})
            role = msg.get("role")
            content = msg.get("content")
            ts = obj.get("timestamp", "")
            # Convert ts string to epoch-ish for sorting (ISO)
            text_parts = []
            if isinstance(content, str):
                text_parts.append(content)
            elif isinstance(content, list):
                for c in content:
                    ctype = c.get("type") if isinstance(c, dict) else None
                    if ctype == "text":
                        text_parts.append(c.get("text", ""))
                    elif ctype == "thinking":
                        # skip thinking
                        pass
                    elif ctype == "tool_use":
                        name = c.get("name", "")
                        inp = c.get("input", {})
                        # Compact tool call summary
                        try:
                            inp_str = json.dumps(inp, indent=2)
                        except:
                            inp_str = str(inp)
                        if len(inp_str) > 1500:
                            inp_str = inp_str[:1500] + "\n... [truncated]"
                        text_parts.append(f"[tool_use: {name}]\n```json\n{inp_str}\n```")
                    elif ctype == "tool_result":
                        # Skip - too noisy
                        pass
            text = "\n\n".join(t for t in text_parts if t)
            if not text:
                continue
            responses_by_session[sid].append({
                "ts": ts,
                "role": role,
                "text": text,
            })

# Sort
for sid in responses_by_session:
    responses_by_session[sid].sort(key=lambda r: r["ts"])

# 3. Build session metadata: earliest timestamp for ordering
session_first_ts = {}
for sid, ps in prompts_by_session.items():
    if ps:
        session_first_ts[sid] = ps[0]["ts"]
for sid, rs in responses_by_session.items():
    if rs and sid not in session_first_ts:
        # parse ISO time
        try:
            session_first_ts[sid] = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(rs[0]["ts"].replace("Z","+00:00")).timestamp() * 1000
        except:
            session_first_ts[sid] = 0

all_sids = sorted(session_first_ts.keys(), key=lambda s: session_first_ts[s])

def fmt_epoch_ms(ms):
    try:
        return datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(ms/1000.0).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    except:
        return str(ms)

def fmt_iso(s):
    try:
        return datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z","+00:00")).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC")
    except:
        return s

# 4. Compose markdown
lines = []
lines.append("# Berzerk Repository — Session History")
lines.append("")
lines.append("Compiled from Claude Code logs at `~/.claude/history.jsonl` (user prompts) and")
lines.append("`~/.claude/projects/-Users-sudnya-checkout-smi-gfx-challenge/<sessionId>.jsonl` (full")
lines.append("conversations, where available).")
lines.append("")
lines.append(f"- Project path: `{PROJECT_PATH}`")
lines.append(f"- Total sessions: {len(all_sids)}")
lines.append(f"- Total user prompts captured: {sum(len(p) for p in prompts_by_session.values())}")
lines.append(f"- Sessions with full assistant transcripts: {sum(1 for s in all_sids if responses_by_session.get(s))}")
lines.append("")
lines.append("Older sessions (pre-format change) only retain user prompts in the global history;")
lines.append("their assistant responses are not recoverable. Sub-agent traces exist for some")
lines.append("of those sessions but are not included here.")
lines.append("")
lines.append("---")
lines.append("")

for idx, sid in enumerate(all_sids, 1):
    ps = prompts_by_session.get(sid, [])
    rs = responses_by_session.get(sid, [])
    first_ts = session_first_ts[sid]

    lines.append(f"- User prompts: {len(ps)}")
    lines.append(f"- Assistant transcript available: {'yes' if rs else 'no (prompts only)'}")
    lines.append("")
    if rs:

        lines.append("### Full transcript")
        lines.append("")
        for entry in rs:
            role = entry["role"]
            text = entry["text"]
            ts = fmt_iso(entry["ts"])
            heading = "User" if role == "user" else "Assistant"
            lines.append(f"#### {heading} — {ts}")
            lines.append("")
            # Use blockquote for user, plain for assistant
            if role == "user":
                for ln in text.splitlines() or [""]:
                    lines.append(f"> {ln}")
                lines.append("")
            else:
                lines.append(text)
                lines.append("")
    else:
        # Prompts only
        lines.append("### User prompts (chronological)")
        lines.append("")
        for i, p in enumerate(ps, 1):
            ts = fmt_epoch_ms(p["ts"])
            lines.append(f"#### Prompt {i} — {ts}")
            lines.append("")
            for ln in (p["text"] or "").splitlines() or [""]:
                lines.append(f"> {ln}")
            lines.append("")
            if p["pasted"]:
                for pid, pdata in (p["pasted"] or {}).items():
                    if isinstance(pdata, dict):
                        ptype = pdata.get("type", "text")
                        pcontent = pdata.get("content", "")
                        lines.append(f"<details><summary>Pasted content #{pid} ({ptype})</summary>")
                        lines.append("")
                        lines.append("```")
                        lines.append(pcontent)
                        lines.append("```")
                        lines.append("")
                        lines.append("</details>")
                        lines.append("")
    lines.append("---")
    lines.append("")

out_text = "\n".join(lines)
with open(OUT, "w") as f:
    f.write(out_text)

print(f"Wrote {OUT}")
print(f"Size: {os.path.getsize(OUT)} bytes")
print(f"Lines: {len(lines)}")

The Makefile change implies Phase 6 (cosimulation) scaffolding is now in place. Concretely:

- A new `cosim-test` target builds a separate test binary from `cosim_test.cpp` + `cosim.cpp` + `cosim_harness.cpp`, mirroring the existing `z80_test` pattern.
- Line 109's exclusion is purely defensive plumbing: `cosim_test.cpp` has its own `main()`, so it must be filtered out of the main emulator link to avoid duplicate-symbol errors. The change itself adds no functionality — it just keeps the main emulator build green now that Phase 6 sources are being tangled into `src/`.
- Architecturally, cosim is being treated as a parallel test harness (own binary, own ROM input, runnable via `make docker-cosim-test`), not as runtime instrumentation woven into the main emulator. So Phase 6 milestones should be tracked against that harness binary, not against `gfx-challenge`/`berzerk` itself.

What it does **not** imply: that the cosim harness actually works yet. The exclusion filter being in place is necessary but not sufficient — the milestone is "scaffolding compiles cleanly alongside main build," not "cosim validates the emulator."

content.text:
Honest assessment: **the Makefile one-liner itself is self-consistent, but I have not verified it builds, and there are landmines in the surrounding untracked files.** Per your global rule I will not commit anything; this is just my read.

What's good about the change:
- Targets `cosim-test` and `docker-cosim-test` already exist (Makefile:161-190) and reference `cosim.cpp`, `cosim_harness.cpp`, `cosim_test.cpp`.
- Matching noweb sources exist: `noweb/cosim.nw`, `noweb/cosim_harness.nw`, `noweb/cosim_test.nw`.
- The exclusion is necessary — `cosim_test.cpp` has its own `main()`, so without it the main `build` target would fail to link.

What I have NOT verified:
- That `make build` (main emulator) still links cleanly after tangle.
- That `make cosim-test` actually compiles end-to-end. The `.nw` files exist on disk but I haven't confirmed the tangled C++ is well-formed against the current `z80.h`/`memory.h` interfaces.

Concrete concerns about the working tree if you stage broadly:
- **`rom/berzerk/` contains the original 1980 Stern Berzerk ROMs.** Copyrighted. These should not be in a public commit. `.gitignore` does not currently exclude `rom/` — that is a real gap. Before any commit I would add `rom/` to `.gitignore`.
- `rom/asteroid` is also untracked — same issue if it's MAME ROM material.
- `SESSION_SUMMARY.md` (192 lines) and `session_history.md` (1385 lines) look like duplicates of `session_status.md` (1199 lines, the one your CLAUDE.md actually mandates). Worth deciding which is the canonical one and deleting the other two rather than committing all three.

Suggested next step before you commit: run `make build` and `make cosim-test` (or their docker variants) to confirm green, and add `rom/` plus the redundant session files to `.gitignore`. Want me to run those builds?

all_records.title: Skip cosim test from main build

content.text:
Both green:

**`make build`** linked `build/berzerk` cleanly with SDL2. The line 109 filter behaved exactly as intended — `cosim_test.cpp` was excluded.

**`make cosim-test`** built `build/cosim_test` and the runtime tests all pass:
- RNG test: PASS
- Maze generation: 6/6 rooms deterministic, PASS
- Maze vs emulator cross-validation: VRAM matches exactly, PASS

So the Makefile change is correct and the cosim infrastructure works end-to-end.

**One design observation worth raising before you commit, though:** the build output shows `cosim.cpp` and `cosim_harness.cpp` are now being linked into the main `berzerk` binary (the filter at line 109 only excludes `*_test.cpp`). That means cosim runtime code ships with production. If that's intentional (e.g., cosim is a runtime-instrumentation hook), fine. If you wanted cosim strictly isolated to the test binary, you'd need to also exclude `cosim.cpp` and `cosim_harness.cpp` from the main `build` target. Worth a 30-second think before committing.

**Can you commit?** Per your global rule, I won't run `git commit` — that's on you. From a build/test correctness standpoint, **yes, the Makefile change itself is safe to commit.** But if you're about to `git add -A`, do these first:

1. Add `rom/` to `.gitignore` (the 1980 Stern Berzerk ROMs are copyrighted — committing them would be a real problem).
2. Decide what to do with `SESSION_SUMMARY.md` and `session_history.md` — they look redundant with `session_status.md`, which is the one your CLAUDE.md mandates.
3. Decide whether to also exclude `cosim.cpp`/`cosim_harness.cpp` from the main build (the design question above).

If you stage selectively (`git add Makefile` only), points 1–2 don't matter for this commit. Point 3 still does.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.

- review: Review a pull request

{
